questions.question: The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted British subsidiary alliance under ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Wellesley**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Subsidiary Alliance** was a policy introduced by **Lord Wellesley**, who served as the Governor-General of India from **1798 to 1805**. This policy was aimed at extending British control over the Indian princely states.
 
• The main feature of this policy was that the Indian rulers had to accept British forces to be stationed within their territories and pay for their maintenance. In return, they would receive protection from external threats and internal revolts.
 
• The **Nizam of Hyderabad** was the first Indian ruler to accept the Subsidiary Alliance in **1798**. This made Hyderabad a dependent ally of the British Empire, and the Nizam ceded control over his foreign relations to the British. *Hence, the correct answer is Lord Wellesley.*
 
• The acceptance of the alliance by the Nizam marked a significant milestone in British expansionism in India, as it allowed them to establish a firm foothold in southern India. This was also a strategic move to counter threats from other powers like the French.
 
• Under the terms of the Subsidiary Alliance, the Nizam agreed to disband his existing army and rely solely on the British forces for protection. This severely limited his sovereignty and made Hyderabad a satellite state of the British Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance:**

 
 
• This was a diplomatic strategy by **Lord Wellesley** to expand British influence in India without direct annexation. It enabled the British to control the foreign policies of Indian rulers while reducing their military capabilities.
 
• Under this alliance, Indian rulers were required to station British troops in their territories and pay for their upkeep. Failure to pay would result in the cession of territory.
 
• **Example:** Apart from Hyderabad, other states like Mysore, Tanjore, and Awadh also accepted the Subsidiary Alliance.
 
 
 
• **Lord Wellesley:**
 
 
• He was the **Governor-General of India** from **1798 to 1805**. Known for his aggressive expansionist policies, he aimed to establish British supremacy in India through treaties and alliances.
 
• The Subsidiary Alliance was one of his most significant policies, which allowed the British to exercise indirect control over Indian states.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Subsidiary Alliance:**
 
 
• It increased British control and influence in India. However, it weakened the Indian rulers militarily and financially, making them dependent on the British.
 
• It paved the way for further annexations and the eventual establishment of British rule over most of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The Indian ruler had to disband his own army and rely on British troops for protection.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for a bicameral Parliament of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 79**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 79 of the Indian Constitution does indeed establish the bicameral nature of the Indian Parliament.
 
 
• The Indian Parliament is a bicameral legislature which consists of two houses: the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People), along with the President of India.
 
• The President has the power to summon and preside over the sessions of both the houses, and he or she can also dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Article 80**: This Article states that the Rajya Sabha will consist of not more than 250 members. Out of these, 12 are nominated by the President from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in the fields of literature, science, art, and social service, and the rest represent the States and Union territories.
 
• **Article 81**: This Article provides for the composition of the Lok Sabha. The House of the People or Lok Sabha consists of representatives directly elected by people of the territorial constituencies in the states and Union territories. As per the amendment of 1977, the Lok Sabha shall consist of not more than 552 members - up to 530 members to represent the territorial constituencies in the States, up to 20 members from Union Territories.
 
• **Article 83**: It determines the duration of the Houses of Parliament. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution. However, Lok Sabha is elected for five years but can be dissolved earlier by the President.
 
• **Article 85**: Gives the President the right to summon each House at such intervals that there shouldn't be more than six months gap between the two sessions. Hence the parliament must meet at least twice a year.
 
• **Article 86**: Gives the President the right to address and send messages to either House of Parliament.

The Constitution of India therefore, in its Articles 79 to 122, provides detailed provisions for the organization, composition, duration, officers, procedures, privileges, and so on for the Parliament in India. The Parliament plays a critical role in the Indian democracy and has substantial legislative, executive, and financial powers. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 49**: This Article falls under the DPSP section of the Constitution. It states that it shall be the obligation of the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest, declared by or under law made by Parliament to be of national importance, from spoliation, disfigurement, destruction, removal, disposal or export, as the case may be.
 
• **Article 59**: This Article deals with the conditions of the President's office. It states that the President shall not be a member of either house of the Parliament or of a house of the legislature of any State, and if any such member is elected President, they shall be deemed to have vacated their seat in that house on the date on which they enter upon their office as President. Additionally, the President shall not hold any other office of profit.
 
• **Article 89**: Article 89 of the Constitution discusses the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, or the Rajya Sabha (Upper House). It states that the council of states will choose one of its members to be the Deputy Chairman whenever the position becomes vacant, and the chosen member will perform the duties of the Chairman when the position of Chairman is vacant or when the Vice-President is acting as, or discharging the functions of, the President.

questions.question: To constitutionally continue holding office, a Minister who is not a member of Parliament at the time of appointment must get elected to either House within ______.

__
 
• Article 75(5) of the Indian Constitution states that a Minister who is not a member of Parliament at the time of appointment must get elected to either House of Parliament within **6 months** to continue holding office.
 
• This provision ensures that individuals holding ministerial positions have democratic legitimacy and accountability by being elected representatives.
 
• If the Minister fails to get elected within six months, he/she must vacate the position immediately as per constitutional requirements.

• **Main Theme: Ministerial Appointment and Democratic Accountability**
 
 
• The appointment of Ministers who are not members of Parliament is allowed under the Indian Constitution but comes with the condition of democratic validation.

questions.question: Which type of reaction is involved in the rusting of iron?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Redox**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rusting of iron** is a chemical process where iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form **iron oxides**, commonly called rust.
 
• This reaction involves both **oxidation** and **reduction**, hence it is categorized as a **redox reaction**.
 
• The **oxidation process** involves the loss of electrons by iron (Fe) as it forms ferrous (Fe²⁺) or ferric (Fe³⁺) ions.
 
• The **reduction process** involves oxygen being reduced by gaining electrons to form hydroxide ions (OH⁻) in the presence of water.
 
• The overall reaction can be written as:

 **4Fe + 3O₂ + 6H₂O → 4Fe(OH)₃**, which eventually dehydrates to form rust (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O).
 
• **Moisture and oxygen** are crucial for the rusting process, which is why it occurs more rapidly in humid environments.
 
• The formation of rust weakens the iron structure, causing damage to its strength and durability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Displacement Reaction**__

 __
 
• A displacement reaction occurs when a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. For example, **Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu**.
 
• Rusting is not a displacement reaction as no exchange or replacement of elements occurs during the process.
 
 
 
• **Combination Reaction**__
 __
 
• In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single product. For example, **2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O**.
 
• Rusting is not a combination reaction because multiple reactions occur simultaneously, and it is not limited to just combining reactants into one product.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition Reaction**__
 
 
• A decomposition reaction involves the breakdown of a compound into two or more substances. For example, **CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂**.
 
• Rusting is not a decomposition reaction, as it involves the formation of new compounds (iron oxides) rather than breaking down existing compounds.
